column1: # v80 ALLOWLIST — the lines in the shipped tree that match a history pattern
# and are allowed to.
# Ian Howell — Embodied Music Lab — GPL-3.0-or-later
# v80 fails on any comment line in a shipped file that narrates the history of
# the code instead of describing it. Some legitimate prose collides with those
# patterns anyway — most often by naming a developer file whose NAME contains
# one of them. Such a line is excused HERE, in writing, with a reason, and
# never by loosening the pattern: a pattern loosened once excuses everything
# shaped like the one line it was loosened for, silently and forever.
# THREE COLUMNS, TAB SEPARATED:
#   path     repository-relative path, exact. No globs — an allowlist that can
#            match a file that does not exist yet is not an allowlist.
#   pattern  R regular expression (perl) matched against the whole line. Make
#            it specific enough to fail if the line is rewritten, because the
#            justification is about THAT line and not about the file.
#   why      one line. If it cannot be said in one line it is not an exception,
#            it is a disagreement with the rule.
# AN ENTRY THAT MATCHES NOTHING IS A FAILURE, not a no-op. A stale exception is
# worse than a missing one: a reader who finds it here believes the tree still
# holds the line it excuses, and a future line that happens to match it is
# excused by a justification written about something else.
plugin/README.md
column3: The README's file map names the files in the folder; naming dev/FIX_NOTES.md is a statement about where a file is, not a history note in a shipped header.
